timeline.message: Support index sorting with nested fields

timeline.body:
This PR piggy-backs on recent changes in Lucene 9.11.1 (https://github.com/apache/lucene/pull/12829, https://github.com/apache/lucene/pull/13341/), setting the parent doc when nested fields are present. This allows moving nested documents along with parent ones during sorting.

With this change, sorting is now allowed on fields outside nested objects. Sorting on fields within nested objects is still not supported (throws an exception).

Fixes #107349
nit: I'd remove the first sentence, it's a bit misleading and the second sentence explains the limitation in a more "positive" way.
timeline.diff_hunk:
@@ -6,9 +6,8 @@ inside each Shard will be sorted. By default Lucene does not apply any sort.
 The `index.sort.*` settings define which fields should be used to sort the documents inside each Segment.
 
 [WARNING]
-nested fields are not compatible with index sorting because they rely on the assumption
-that nested documents are stored in contiguous doc ids, which can be broken by index sorting.
-An error will be thrown if index sorting is activated on an index that contains nested fields.
+Nested fields are not compatible with index sorting. It is allowed to apply index sorting to mappings

timeline.body: I wonder how this works when the nested field is added as an update to the mapping? Should we always set the parent field in case a nested field is added later?

reply.body: Good point, I was thinking about this but wasn't sure of the implications. @jpountz any thoughts on this?
I asked a similar question to @s1monw a while back, and he suggested always adding the parent field when an index sort is configured.
Excellent, this simplifies things. Lemme update the PR.
Maybe include the reason why parent field is always enabled in the comment too?
Right, this was added in the last iteration.

timeline.body:
So happy to see this resolved @kkrik-es !
I left a question regarding the handling of new nested fields in existing mapping.

timeline.body: I wonder if we need to keep this limitation for existing index? This would mean checking the index version to ensure that this mode is not activated on indices with an index sort and already indexed documents.

reply.body: I see, the problem is that existing indexes do not have the parent field set and a mapping update may introduce a nested object. That's correct, we need to check for the version here.
